title: Denouement (85-90 minutes)
use_cases: Configure when drafting the final 5-10 minutes of a script to establish narrative resolution
Implement when planning a sequel by leaving specific lore-based plot threads unresolved
Use when providing a emotional arc conclusion where the protagonist is permanently altered
Configure when adding a post-climax jump scare to maintain audience tension
content:
Aftermath: The protagonist either survives, but is deeply changed by the experience, or succumbs to the horror.

Final twist or scare: Many horror films end with a twist that implies the horror isn’t fully over (e.g., Carrie’s hand reaching from the grave) or leaves the door open to a potential sequel.

Example: In “From Dusk Till Dawn” (1996), criminal Seth and his hostage Kate survive, but they have lost their loved ones. As Seth drives away, leaving Kate on her own, we see the back of the Titty Twister bar (the vampires’ lair) for the first time. The camera pulls away, revealing that the bar is built on top of an ancient Aztec temple and hinting at the deeper, ongoing horror that remains. This leaves the door open for potential sequels and a lingering sense of dread.
